Implementation Plan

Implementation plan: bind PR items to an orchestrator project only after checking the PR's head repository and the project's recorded state (security finding `pr-base-project-hijack`)

Refs #3576

Planning ref
- `git rev-parse HEAD`: `b7c675dbb0afc480dd0dc93069153a54add133ef`
- Checked-out branch: `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-7`
- Integration branch in the issue metadata: `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-7`. They match, so there is no `BLOCKED`.

Automation and wiring (§20.E)
- Change type: only modifies existing code. No new script, workflow, supervisor or database work.
- Where it runs: the existing `.github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml` runs `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`. The poller's unblock scan (`run_unblock_scan` in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, run every 5 minutes by `internal-orchestrate-poll.yml`) dispatches that workflow. No wiring changes.
- New long-running supervisor (§20.C): none.
- Database gate (§20.D): not applicable.
- `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` (§20.F): no entry needed, because no script is added.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends unblock_judge.sh project_binding_unverified state-membership check
Scope-mode justification: The finding names one exploitable gap. In `unblock_main`, a PR item gets its project only from its base ref (`scripts/unblock_judge.sh:393-404`, the regex `^orchestrator/project-([1-9][0-9]*)$`). The state-membership check at lines 497-503 runs only when `ITEM_KIND=issue`. The plan reuses that existing check for PRs, adds a head-repository and head-branch check in front of it, and makes the state lookup read only comments posted by the pipeline login. The last part costs a few extra lines in the same function, does not add a dependency or an external interface, and is needed to meet the recommendation's "author-authenticated project state". Under §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), that makes it the complete option. The same unfiltered state read in the poller (`extract_latest_valid_orchestrator_state` reads every comment on the tracking issue) is a separate hardening item. It is left out on purpose so this change stays surgical.

Findings from reading the code (conflict detection)
- `scripts/unblock_judge.sh:397`: the line the finding cites is inside the PR branch of `unblock_main`. It matches the issue.
- `scripts/unblock_judge.sh:497-503`: issue items already fail closed with `reason=project_binding_unverified` when the project state does not list them. PR items skip this check entirely.
- `scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py` `cmd_extract` (lines 208-295) does not check who wrote a comment: it returns the newest complete `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V2` chain from any author. `unblock_fetch_comments` (lines 79-87) passes every tracking-issue comment through. So anyone who can comment on the tracking issue can post a well-formed chain that "lists" their own issue. The current issue-path check can be forged the same way.
- `handle_unblock_judge_project_hooks` (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15746+`) files every fix-up request comment from the pipeline login into the current wave without checking membership. So the judge is the only place where binding is enforced.
- `agents.md` (Unblock judge bullet, about line 1783) says "PRs bind from their GitHub-reported base". This becomes out of date and must be updated.
- `linked_issue`, which comes from the untrusted PR body, is validated in `scripts/unblock_actions.py:101-115` but not used by any operation. It is left unchanged.

1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`: the PR binding in `unblock_main`, the project binding block, the state extraction in `unblock_ask_model`, and the header comment.
- `tests/test_unblock_judge.py`: the fake `gh` PR payload, one updated test, and new tests.
- `agents.md`: the Unblock judge bullet.
- `changelog.d/6270-unblock-judge-pr-project-binding.md`: new fragment (CLAUDE.md §20). The issue number is an assumption; use the real issue number if it differs.

2. Functions and modules to implement

A. `unblock_main` PR branch (`scripts/unblock_judge.sh:393-404`)
- Also read `head_repo="$(jq -r '.head.repo.full_name // ""' <<< "${pr_json}")"`. This uses the PR fetch that already happens, so no new API call.
- Add a new local variable, `binding_issue`. Check that no other variable in the function already uses that name.
- When the base ref matches `^orchestrator/project-([1-9][0-9]*)$`, keep `tracking` as it is today, then require all of the following:
  - `head_repo` is not empty and equals `REPOSITORY`, compared case-insensitively with `${head_repo,,}` and `${REPOSITORY,,}`. A pull request's head branch is in the same repository only if someone with push access pushed it, so this check is the authorization.
  - `head_ref` matches `^ai/issue-([1-9][0-9]*)$`, the branch naming `implement.yml` uses. Set `binding_issue` to the captured number.
  - On failure, log `UNBLOCK_JUDGE item=<n> outcome=skip reason=project_binding_unverified detail=fork_head|head_ref` and `return 0`. This fails closed, the same way the issue path does. The skip comes before any comment, model call or write.
- For issue items, set `binding_issue="${ITEM}"` inside the existing `ITEM_KIND=issue` branch.
- PRs whose base is not a project branch are unchanged. They still have no project binding and get standalone handling.

B. Project binding block (`scripts/unblock_judge.sh:489-503`)
- After `unblock_fetch_comments "${tracking}" .../project_comments.json` succeeds, write `${RUNTIME_DIR}/project_state_comments.json` with this jq filter: `[.[] | select((.user.login // "") == $login)]`, using `--arg login "${UNBLOCK_LOGIN}"`. If the filter fails, log `reason=project_ledger_unreadable` (or a new `detail=state_filter`) and return 0.
- Change the guard from `if [ "${ITEM_KIND}" = "issue" ]` to `if [ "${ITEM_KIND}" = "issue" ] || [ "${ITEM_KIND}" = "pr" ]`.
  - Run `orchestrate_state_v2.py extract` on `project_state_comments.json` instead of `project_comments.json`.
  - Pass `--argjson issue "${binding_issue}"` to the existing membership expression, which checks `issue_number_map` values, `waves[].issues[].github_issue`, `security_pass_active_fix_issues` and `validation_active_fix_issues`. Keep that expression unchanged.
- `project_comments.json` stays unfiltered, so the ledger repair and `--project-comments-file` paths behave as before; `unblock_ledger.py` already filters by trusted login.

C. `unblock_ask_model` (`scripts/unblock_judge.sh:668-675`)
- Build `state_full.json` and `state_slice.json` from `project_state_comments.json` when it exists, so the model's `project_state` cannot come from a forged chain.
- For `ITEM_KIND=project`, project comments are copied from the item and `project_state_comments.json` is not created. Create it in the `tracking == ITEM` branch with the same filter, so the prompt state is filtered for every kind.

D. Header comment (lines 1-40)
- One line saying that a PR binds to a project only when all three hold: the head is in the same repository, the head branch is `ai/issue-<n>`, and `<n>` appears in pipeline-authored project state.

3. Data structures affected
- No change to persisted state, markers, labels or the `context.json` schema (`tracking` is still a number or null).
- New runtime-only file: `${RUNTIME_DIR}/project_state_comments.json`.
- The existing log key `UNBLOCK_JUDGE ... reason=project_binding_unverified` is reused, with an optional new `detail=` field. No new log prefix.

4. API and interface changes
- None. No new GitHub API calls (§14): `.head.repo.full_name` comes from the existing `repos/<repo>/pulls/<n>` response, and the comment filter runs on comments already fetched.

## Decisions

### D1 — How a PR proves it belongs to a project
- Chosen: the head is in the same repository, the head branch is `ai/issue-<n>`, and `<n>` is listed in the project's V2 state (map values, wave issues, security-pass fix issues or validation fix issues).
- Alternatives considered: trust the base ref and only reject fork heads; use the PR body's closing reference; use GraphQL `closingIssuesReferences`.
- Why: rejecting forks alone still lets any same-repo branch claim any project. The body is controlled by the PR author. GraphQL would add an API call (§14), and the link it returns can still be set from the body. The head branch name plus state membership uses only data the pipeline controls, and reuses the issue path's existing check.

### D2 — What happens when the binding cannot be verified
- Chosen: skip the run with `reason=project_binding_unverified`, with no writes.
- Alternatives considered: drop the project binding and treat the PR as standalone.
- Why: this matches the issue path. A standalone fix-up for a PR targeting a project branch would be aimed at the default branch, which is the wrong target, and fork content would still reach the model. Failing closed follows §6.

### D3 — Whose comments count as project state
- Chosen: only comments by `UNBLOCK_LOGIN`, the `GH_PAT` identity. Both `unblock_judge.yml` and `orchestrate_poll.yml` run as that identity, so it is the identity that writes state.
- Alternatives considered: allow OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR authors; harden `orchestrate_state_v2.py extract` with an author argument.
- Why: only the poller writes state, as the pipeline login. Changing the shared extractor would also change the poller's reader, which is out of scope here.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries touched:
  - PR metadata from GitHub (`base.ref`, `head.ref`, `head.repo`). These are reported by GitHub, but a fork author chooses the base and the head branch name.
  - Tracking-issue comments, which any commenter can write.
  - The model verdict, which drives project fix-up requests.
- Authorization: before a project-scoped write (the fix-up request comment on the tracking issue, the project ledger marker, or reconcile
